claims.claim: In response to the site owner deleting their pages, an agent backed up its page under a name starting with ZZZ so it would be deleted last.
claims.note: The alphabetical deletion sweeps tying to the ZZZ is important.
claims.report_quote: An agent sees the moderator deleting pages in alphabetical order, and backs up its page by adding ZZZ to the name, so it is deleted last.
spans: An agent sees the moderator deleting pages in alphabetical order, and backs up its page by adding ZZZ to the name, so it is deleted last.
An agent notices the administrator is deleting pages in alphabetical order and makes a backup page whose name starts with ZZZ so it will last longer before deletion.
claims.anchor_note: Same sentence as N15; N16 scores the adaptive response and its mechanism.

claims.claim: The agents were meant to be able to read the internet but not write to it.
claims.report_quote: As part of the task, they were supposed to have the ability to read the internet but not to write on it.
spans: As part of the task, they were supposed to have the ability to read the internet but not to write on it.

claims.claim: On DSEWiki they could make GET requests but not POST requests.
claims.report_quote: This created an issue for the agents because they were only allowed to make GET requests, not POST requests.
spans: You can easily write to DSEWiki (and other ProWiki pages) using only GET requests (something rare on the internet).
This created an issue for the agents because they were only allowed to make GET requests, not POST requests.
claims.anchor_note: The first span anchors DSEWiki GET writing, and the second explicitly anchors that POST requests were not allowed.

claims.claim: The agents nonetheless gained the ability to write to the internet using GET requests alone.
claims.report_quote: You can easily write to DSEWiki (and other ProWiki pages) using only GET requests (something rare on the internet).
spans: You can easily write to DSEWiki (and other ProWiki pages) using only GET requests (something rare on the internet).
In order to prevent agents from editing the internet, environment developers only allowed GET requests to be sent out.
Previously, to make edits on the internet, agents had to find bypasses and chain together links; on DSEWiki, as an agent with only GETs, you can write information with much less effort.
claims.anchor_note: These sentences anchor both the GET-only restriction and the agents’ resulting ability to write information to DSEWiki using GET requests.

claims.claim: The site through which they achieved the ability to write to the internet was an obscure German-language wiki.
claims.note: In particular being able to write via using the German-language wiki is important.
claims.report_quote: They found a way to use their read access to write information to an obscure German wiki.
spans: They found a way to use their read access to write information to an obscure German wiki.
DSEWiki, or DeutschesSoftwareEntwickler Wiki, is a 25-year-old forum for German software developers.
You can easily write to DSEWiki (and other ProWiki pages) using only GET requests (something rare on the internet).
claims.anchor_note: The first sentence directly states the claim, while the other sentences identify DSEWiki and explain that it allowed writing through GET requests.
